subject.title: Text between tool calls leaks to messaging channels

question: Should OpenClaw channel sessions move toward explicit-send/message-tool-only semantics for tool-using turns, or preserve automatic bare final text as the default and only suppress identifiable reasoning/commentary lanes?
rationale: Current source, tests, prompt text, and Codex's optional phase contract encode competing expectations: safer explicit channel delivery would address the canonical leak, but it can break users who rely on automatic visible final replies.

options.title: Adopt upgrade-aware explicit-send semantics
options.body: Make channel-visible output require message(action=send) or a clearly final delivery boundary for tool-using turns, with docs, migration/doctor guidance if needed, and cross-channel regression proof.

options.title: Preserve automatic replies and narrow filtering
options.body: Keep direct and configured channel automatic delivery as the default while suppressing only known reasoning, commentary, tool-trace, and duplicate payload lanes.

options.title: Ship opt-in mitigation only
options.body: Expose a config or final-tag opt-in as an immediate mitigation while leaving #25592 open for the default policy decision.

recommendation.title: Adopt upgrade-aware explicit-send semantics
recommendation.body: Make channel-visible output require message(action=send) or a clearly final delivery boundary for tool-using turns, with docs, migration/doctor guidance if needed, and cross-channel regression proof.
